title: Why Climate Never Sits Still
question: What makes Earth's climate shift beyond everyday weather?
hook: A volcano, a cloudless year and a warming ocean all nudge the climate, but on very different clocks.
idea: Climate varies through internal shifts of energy and external forcing, and slow parts like oceans stretch short pushes into long swings.

beats.prompt: Sort each cause of climate variability into its group.
beats.explain: Internal variability comes from natural processes within the climate system moving energy around, while external forcing comes from events outside the system's components.

beats.prompt: For several years, more energy reaches Earth from the sun than leaves it for space. What happens to the climate system?

choices.label: It cools
choices.feedback: Cooling happens when more energy goes out than comes in, the reverse of this case.

choices.label: It stays the same
choices.feedback: An imbalance in the energy budget changes the climate; it does not leave it unchanged.

beats.explain: When incoming energy is greater than outgoing energy, the energy budget is positive and the climate system warms.

beats.prompt: Match each process to how it plays out.
pairs: Weather, seen from a climate view
beats.explain: Parts of the climate system respond at very different speeds, from fast volcanic cooling to ocean expansion lasting thousands of years.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A year has few clouds, creating an energy imbalance.
Extra heat is absorbed by the oceans.
Because the ocean reacts quickly, the heat is gone within days and leaves no trace.
So a short weather quirk can show up as longer-lasting variability.
beats.explain: Climate inertia lets the signal be stored in the ocean and expressed on longer time scales than the original weather disturbance.
